text:
John Carlson spent 1,143 games in Washington, won a Stanley Cup there in 2018, and is now 36 and playing for Tampa Bay after a short stop in Anaheim. He is giving the Lightning exactly what they wanted. On Nov. 11 in Buffalo he had a career-best five points in an 8-3 win and passed 800 career points ("You never take anything for granted," as RMNB's headline quoted him).

The season numbers hold up beyond that night. He has 16 points in 20 games, and the Lightning take 60.07% of expected goals at 5v5 with him on, 5.87 points better than without him. That fits what Evolving-Hockey saw last season, when he ranked 17th among defensemen in wins above replacement and drove play in the 93rd percentile.

The six goals are a little lucky: 12.5% shooting against a talent range closer to 8%, on 3.9 expected goals. He also plays fewer minutes than he used to, about 19 a night. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking flagged his weak spot, exits under a forecheck, where only 31% kept possession. As a puck mover at this stage of his career, he has been very good.
headline: John Carlson, 800 points and a fresh start in Tampa
